meta.name: Small-Space Gardening
meta.author: OUTSIDE//OS Core Team & Hacktoberfest Contributors
meta.description: Cultivating soil vitality, balcony containers, window boxes, and micro-gardens with minimal equipment.
safety_guidelines: Always wash hands after touching garden compost or potting soil.
Never lean out over balcony railings or place unanchored pots where they could fall.
Check pots for stinging insects or spiders before reaching inside.

quests.title: Balcony Micro-Soil Health & Moisture Check
quests.objective: Audit soil texture, drainage, and root moisture across 2 to 3 outdoor containers or balcony pots.
quests.suitability_reason: Perfect for apartment dwellers or container gardeners with 15 minutes of outdoor balcony time.

steps.instruction: Step out to your balcony, patio, or window sill planters.
steps.detail: Inspect container saucers: is there standing water or bone-dry sediment?

steps.instruction: Insert your index finger 2 centimeters into the topsoil of each pot.
steps.detail: Assess whether moisture is cool and crumbly, muddy and waterlogged, or hard-packed and hydrophobic.

steps.instruction: Inspect the base of plant stems for soil compaction or salt crusting from tap water minerals.
steps.detail: Gently loosen compacted surface crust with a twig or finger without damaging surface feeder roots.

checklist: Checked moisture depth of at least two pots
Inspected drainage holes for blockages or root bound escaping tips
Cleared away dried, decaying dead leaves from soil surface
quests.bonus_challenge: Identify which planter receives the most hours of unobstructed daylight.
quests.safe_alternative: Check indoor potted plants or herbs on a kitchen windowsill using the same finger-depth moisture test.
quests.completion_criteria: Inspect and log the hydration state of at least one container.
quests.reflection_question: Did your soil feel cooler or warmer than the ambient outdoor air temperature?
safety_notes: Do not overfill watering cans to avoid spilling water over balcony edges.
Ensure planters are securely fastened against wind gusts.

quests.title: Seed Pod & Leaf Node Scout
quests.objective: Survey plants for reproductive growth: maturing seed heads, flowering nodes, or runners.
quests.suitability_reason: Learn how small-space flora propagates and prepares for future growth cycles.

steps.instruction: Carefully examine foliage stems from the soil line upward.
steps.detail: Look for axillary buds where leaves branch from main stems.

steps.instruction: Find one spent flower blossom or dried pod holding seeds.
steps.detail: Observe the protective shell: is it fuzzy, papery, prickly, or winged?

steps.instruction: Check for natural symbiotic visitors (ladybugs, small bees, spiders).
steps.detail: Watch their interaction without disturbing them.

checklist: Identified a leaf node where new growth or buds originate
Observed a seed capsule or flower structure up close
Noticed whether leaves point towards the sun's current angle
quests.bonus_challenge: Collect one dry fallen seed pod to observe its internal chamber structure.
quests.safe_alternative: Examine a fresh fruit or vegetable in your kitchen (e.g. apple, bell pepper) and observe seed chamber geometry.
quests.completion_criteria: Spot at least one sign of active plant reproduction or new shoot development.
quests.reflection_question: How do the seed pods you observed use geometry to disperse seeds?
safety_notes: Do not ingest unidentified seeds or berries.
Wash hands with soap and water after handling garden pods.
